The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

U.S. Democratic sweep could be the final nail in the ‘Clarity Act’s coffin’. Industry experts warn the Clarity Act is likely dead in its current form as incoming Democratic majorities eye tighter scrutiny of crypto markets and tokenized stocks. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Wall Street rethinks AI data center boom as Texas election raises new risks. Bitcoin miners pivoting to AI face new uncertainty over power access and construction permits, while companies with approved projects could benefit from tighter supply. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto Long & Short: ICE is betting on retail’s appetite for quick outcomes. Retail traders increasingly want trades that resolve fast, from prediction markets to same-day options. Andy Baehr of GSR argues perpetual futures belong in that group, and that ICE’s deal to bring Trade[XYZ]’s Hyperliquid markets onshore is a play for that customer, one that doesn’t need a crypto asset to work. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The election changes Washington. The work on crypto continues. The next Congress inherits an unfinished assignment: establishing clear, lasting rules for digital assets that protect consumers and ensure American innovation continues to thrive, writes Blockchain Association's Lindsay Fraser. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin and stocks post big gains, reversing overnight plunge following Blue Wave landslide. The biggest losers, so far, are the AI data center stocks following victories for several candidates who campaigned expressly against the sector. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Global asset manager Schroders brings emerging market bond fund to Solana. The global asset manager, which oversees $1.1 trillion in assets, is bringing an actively managed bond strategy onchain through tokenization specialist Centrifuge. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $80,118 with a +3.12% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,414.21 with a +5.73% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

# Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows

Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows
John Isige

Bitcoin (BTC) is trading above $81,000 on Tuesday, aligning with a lethargic tone in the broader cryptocurrency market. The support range between $80,000-$81,000 reinforces the prevailing stability and consolidation, prompting institutional inflows. [...] Ethereum spot ETFs, on the other hand, recorded $103 million in outflows on Monday, sustaining a four-day bearish streak. Looking back, since September 29, ETH ETFs have posted only one day of inflows, totaling $25 million on October 13. [...] Institutional investors staged a comeback on Monday, with $527 million in Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), up from roughly $82 million in outflows last Friday. Broadly, cumulative inflows stand at $57.4 billion, with net assets under management at $105 billion, according to SoSoValue data. A steady inflow pattern would cushion Bitcoin against headwinds, increasing the odds of a recovery.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Over the years, Bitcoin ETFs have collected a staggering $57.6 billion in net inflows since their inception, whereas Ethereum funds have garnered $13.8 billion. Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024—about six months before Ethereum funds, which debuted in July 2024.

At the current inflow rate, Ethereum funds are outpacing Bitcoin funds by about $525 million annually. However, it would take more than 80 years to close the existing $44 billion gap in total inflows.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] ## Key Points

 U.S. cryptocurrency regulation is evolving: Federal law now governs stablecoins, while broader legislation defining oversight of digital asset markets remains unresolved.
 Governments globally have adopted widely varying approaches to digital asset regulation, from permissive frameworks to outright bans.
 U.S. oversight is divided among regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, with the IRS treating cryptocurrency as property for federal tax purposes.
